Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes discussed the ongoing events in Iran, where Amir Houieh noted precise attacks against military targets and anticipated a regime change, while they also decided to keep the Civil project cycle monthly for faster progress, differentiating it from the proposed six-week lab cycle suggested by Noémi Biró. The lab website is ready for launch, with Amir Houieh planning to deploy the final changes and Gabor Kerekes confirming domain management under Hussein's Cloudflare account; simultaneously, Gabor Kerekes updated the team on the Mycelium and agent sandbox progress, successfully using the agent for data crawling, and discussed with Noémi Biró the "dog fooding" approach for the agent sandbox before a workshop. Additionally, they reviewed the Minha project, primarily an income source for the lab, and discussed prioritizing Civil planning and efficient workflows with autonomous agents before heavily investing in the Mycelium infrastructure, which Gabor Kerekes described as a dynamic, attention-guiding interface supporting the user's "higher self."
Details
Discussion on Current Events in Iran: The participants discussed the ongoing events in Iran, expressing happiness about the targeted attacks on commanders and military bases (00:00:00). Amir Houieh mentioned that the attacks are very precise, targeting specific rooms or floors of buildings, though they are concerned about the use of hospitals as shelters. The goal of the opposition is to weaken the current power structure by taking away their power and guns, with people waiting for a signal from opposition leaders or Trump to take to the streets (00:04:46). Gabor Kerekes inquired about the potential for regime change and the development of democracy in Iran, to which Amir Houieh responded that they believe the current regime will certainly be replaced (00:05:47).
Lab and Civil Project Cycle Planning: The discussion shifted to planning the timeline for the second project cycle, with Noémi Biró suggesting a six-week duration for the lab, running from March 1st to April 13th, as four weeks seems too short (00:27:05). Gabor Kerekes suggested aligning the lab and Civil project cycles, but Amir Houieh cautioned that the Civil project requires a faster pace, especially initially, to show progress to Melissa and to avoid overspending the budget timeline. They agreed to keep the Civil cycle monthly, perhaps with weekly or bi-weekly small breakdowns (00:27:34).
New Lab Website Launch: The group confirmed that the lab website is finished and ready to go live today. Amir Houieh planned to deploy the final changes at the end of the session, needing to run the metadata generator first (00:28:40). The final steps for going live involve connecting the domain, which Gabor Kerekes noted is managed on Cloudflare under an account owned by Hussein (00:29:58).
Minha Project and Future Plans: The Minha project brief is expected on the 9th of March, and the team will return with questions and planning by the 11th, with the project likely finishing within March (00:32:25) (00:34:24). Noémi Biró asked for clarification on their involvement, and Amir Houieh explained that the project is primarily an income source for the lab and that Noémi Biró's involvement will be limited unless they are specifically needed (00:33:31). Amir Houieh also noted that the "brain" prototype is ready to be tried out today or tomorrow, pending a final cleanup before pushing the code (00:34:24).
Progress on Mycelium and Agent Sandbox: Gabor Kerekes provided an update on working on the mycelium and the agent sandbox, which they believe will be a significant speed multiplier. They anticipate that having an agent running using free Gemini usage via Google Cloud Platform will be beneficial for exploration, as agents can quickly validate different technology choices and stacks. Gabor Kerekes successfully used the agent for a spike that involved crawling a URL, saving the data to a database in about ten minutes (00:35:23).
Planning the Agent Sandbox Workshop: Noémi Biró asked how to proceed with the agent sandbox, suggesting a workshop or a blog post. Gabor Kerekes recommended "dog fooding" the tool first to work out friction points, which means the team should try using it before publishing (00:37:14). They plan to schedule a workshop once the known issues are resolved and the setup is easier for the team (00:38:31).
Discussion on Mycelium Prototype and Next Steps: Amir Houieh requested an update on the mycelium prototype's progress, emphasizing that the mockup is currently more valuable than a working implementation (00:38:31). The team agreed to prioritize planning for Civil and establishing an efficient workflow using autonomous agents before heavily investing in the mycelium infrastructure (00:39:57). They decided to hold a dedicated session after the planning discussion to look at the mycelium update (00:41:16).
Mycelium as a Dynamic Attention-Guiding Interface: Gabor Kerekes provided an overview of the Mycelium project, explaining that it is more than just a bookmarking tool; it is envisioned as a dynamic interface that weaves together bookmarks, cloud conversations, and notes (00:41:16). The system should autonomously figure out how to best represent the data, such as creating an overview of the origin of an idea, the problem space, and the architecture (00:46:41). The system's core function is to direct the user's attention to what is important to them, contrasting with existing software that acts as a "parasite on your attention" (00:48:22).
Mycelium's Role in Supporting the User's "Higher Self": The system is designed to support the user's "wise mind" or "higher self" that makes wise decisions, helping them communicate high-level priorities and values to the system (00:52:16). The system would monitor if the user is living in line with those values and guide their attention accordingly, sometimes even by instructing them to step away from the computer (00:50:19).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will deploy the last changes to the lab website today, including running the metadata generator, so the new website can go live.
Gabor Kerekes will ensure the agent sandbox is working for him and iron out known issues, then conduct a workshop session this week to teach the group how to use it.
Gabor Kerekes will look into transferring the ownership of the Cloudflare account from Hussein's account to someone else.
The group will discuss the Minha project brief after receiving it on March 9th and plan for its completion in March.
You should review Gemini's notes to make sure they're accurate. Get tips and learn how Gemini takes notes
Please provide feedback about using Gemini to take notes in a short survey.
